steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease baking sheets.
Cream the butter with the white sugar and brown sugar. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix the flour and baking powder together. Stir in the flour mixture into the butter mixture and combine.

Form dough into 1 inch balls and place on the prepared baking sheet. Make an indentation in each cookie and fill with jam. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 12 to 15 minutes. Let cool completely and sprinkle with confectioners' sugar.

review.reviewBody: I've made these several times. I turn them into peanut butter and jelly cookies by subbing half of the butter for peanut butter and I use blackberry or boysenberry jelly. They are the best!

What a great way to use up all the extra strawberry preserves! Thanks to all the previous reviews, I added an extra 1/4 cup of flour. It was helpful to use a rounded teaspoon to made an indent in the middle of the cookies, pushing with my other hand the surrounding cookie dough into the teaspoon so that that cookie was nice and tight. For fun i added cocoa powder, which made the cookies nice and chocolatey with the strawberry preserve. I’m glad i found a way to use up preserves, and the family ate it right up. But i wish the surrounding part of the cookie were more flavorful.

The ingredients are simple enough that you could make these for a last minute treat. You do not need to grease the cookie sheet, as these have enough butter in them to not stick to the pan. I used a round teaspoon dipped in sugar to depress the centers with before filling with the jam. These come out perfectly when baked on an airbake sheet. They tend to get too brown on the bottom if you use a regular cookie sheet. It took a while to get the bake time right, but once I did, oh WOW! Wonderfully buttery cookies! I made 2 batches, one with seedless boysenberry preserves, the other with homemade apricot jam. I preferred the apricot, and these got rave reviews at Bunco! I'm making more today!

OMG!! These ae to die for. My husband and I both said these are the absolute best cookies we have ever tasted. Seriously. I followed the recipe exactly and used some Smuckers Black rasberry Simply Fruit spreadable fruit and it worked perfectly. The first time I made them I used another kind of preserves and it was a little more runny. The spreadable fruit is perfect for these cookies. I made the indentation with a 1/2 tsp spoon and filled it with about 1/2 tsp in each cookie. I normally might eat 1 or 2 cookies after I make a batch but these I just can't stop eating. Not sure if that's a good thing. Even the kids kept asking for more and I had to stop them and tell them they have had enough and that is unusual for my kids. Only thing I did was put the dough in the fridge for about 3 minutes which I thik helped keep them from spreading a little and made sure there was a nice deep crater for the jelly so it doesnlt overflow over the side. I baked them about 14 minutes and they are perfect. You will not be disappointed.

This is my favorite Christmas cookie of all time! 
I double the recipe and it made nearly 60 cookies! 
I use the cap from a 1/2 gallon of milk to push down the cookie and make a "well". It's all about the preserves which I alternate between - this time I used Smucker's red raspberry, cherry, blackberry, apricot, and pineapple. Be sure they are preserves if you use regular jam or jelly, it will spill over the cookie - they are still good even if this happens- but the presentation won't be as nice. I don't use the confectioner's sugar. You should make this one!

I've never had so many people ask for my recipe before. The only thing I changed was that I used apricot jam and a few slivers of almonds on top. Yummy. Edited to add that the one sheet that I greased, all baked flat and useless. The pans that I used parchment paper on were perfect.

This is such an easy and tasty cookie! I took the advice of another reviewer and used a small glass, coated the bottom with white sugar and flattened them. I then made a well and used raspberry in half and strawberry in the other half. Baked 15 minutes.

I've made 5 types of cookies this week. THESE ARE MY FAVORITE. An excellent shortbread dough recipe. I used raspberry JAM, and it set up perfectly. I did bake several.mins longer though. In order to store, I definitely sprinkled with powdered sugar AFTER they cooled, so they wouldn't stick together in The tin
I made them and they are sooooo good! I added a pinch of salt and for the jam I made a apple & cinnamon jam (that was really easy to make) over all super yummy!
Great recipe. We have been using it for years. Even at high altitude they turn out delicious. We use a Mellon Baller to create the perfect indent, then use it to portion out the jelly.
These came out very good. Lined baking sheets with parchment paper rather then grease which worked well. Substituted strawberry jam in place of raspberry. Made about 3 dozen.
Made it as instructed. Super simple and tasty. I made grape and Nutella ones.
Delicious cookie and easy recipe! I'll be saving this recipe and making them again! Thank you!
The cookies are easy to make and delicious and so pretty! Will make a great Christmas cookie too!

Amazingly delicious! This was my first time ever making this type of cookie and they came out great. I used the classic taste of strawberry and grape preserves in my cookies and these were a huge hit for my family. Will definitely make again!
Wonderful! I made them as written. Will make again!

I made them just as written and they were delicious. They spread more than I expected, but I let enough room between cookies so that worked out. I made three different flavors ... apricot, raspberry and lemon curd. Will make again!
As a non baker I tried these for a holiday cookie exchange for work. I agree with everyone else, they were easy to make and not overly sweet. 5 stars from me.

I love this recipe! Ended up using 4 different jams I had on hand: Strawberry, Blackberry, Orange Marmalade and Raspberry- yum!Remember to use preserves and not jelly, which is thin and will run out out the indented cookie :-)
